analysis.title: Asia Open - The Fed clears the way for earnings
key_insights: The FOMC left rates unchanged in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed's Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp hike.

The policy statement was largely unchanged. The main edit upgraded the description of economic activity from "solid" to "strong". The committee said accumulating more information will guide the policy stance.
Fed Chair Warsh skewed slightly dovish in the press conference, saying most at the Fed do not think the economy is running hot. The Fed gave no clear signal for December.
UST yields fell about 10bps peak to trough, with a sharp curve steepening led by the front end. The dollar weakened and equities gained into the close.

After-market earnings pulled equities in opposite directions. Alphabet fell 11% after Q3 revenue ex-TAC of $111.2B missed consensus, with declines in search and YouTube. Microsoft rose 3% on strong results.
Oracle rose 11% after its investor day, where management laid out a long-term free cash flow outlook.
The BoC hiked 25bps in line with market expectations but to the surprise of many economists, and CAD strengthened about 0.4%. The BoC framed the hike as risk management.
The dollar weakened on the dovish Warsh press conference and on reports that VP JD Vance reached out to Iranian leadership. DXY traded -0.20% to 102.13 and EURUSD traded at 1.116.

WTI settled at $101 and Brent was little changed at $114, with the spread widening on Gulf Coast pipeline pressures. European TTF gas rose more than 5% through €100 for the first time since December 2022, on heating demand and low stockpiles.
Gold traded higher to $4,066 (+0.2%), recovering earlier losses after the Fed held and gave no clear December signal.
Desk flows were better to buy, with inflows in Info Tech, Healthcare, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials and Energy. Outflows led in Financials and Comm Services.
The G10 FX Strategy desk is short EURNOK as its preferred expression of a EUR-positive view. The ECB is expected to hold on Thursday.

Microsoft reported strong results (10/29 after-market) and the stock rose 3% after-market.

macro_indicators.reading: Rates unchanged, 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25bp hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: The hold was expected. The two hawkish dissents and the "strong" activity upgrade were offset by Warsh's dovish tilt, so yields fell.
The hike matched market expectations but surprised many economists, and CAD strengthened about 0.4%.
The ECB decision comes alongside US Core PCE on Thursday.
Soft trends would reiterate that the Riksbank is unlikely to hike in November. Citi still sees a December hike as plausible depending on inflation.
Market consensus is for a hold.
